title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from 1.8): R is a base, S→R, F is a fibred category over (Sch)/R. Crystals of type F on S relative to R live on the infinitesimal site, with no divided powers. Δ_n is the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in S×_R S. A stratification is a compatible family of n-connections pr1*E ≅ pr2*E satisfying the cocycle condition on the neighbourhoods of the diagonal of S×_R S×_R S. Taking the value at S gives a functor (crystals) → (objects of F_S with stratification). 1.4 showed this functor need not be faithful.

This page states:
(i) The functor is an equivalence when S→R is formally smooth. Examples: S→R smooth, or Spec k → Spec k0 with k/k0 separable.
(ii) If S→R is formally étale, both categories are equivalent to F_S. This recovers the 'exemple à la noix' of 1.5 in characteristic 0.
(iii) A conjecture, explicitly unproved ('Sauf erreur ... je n'ai pas écrit la démonstration'): the equivalence holds for S→R flat and locally of finite presentation. The handwritten addition restricts this to R locally noetherian and coherent modules.

1.9, characteristic 0: if S is smooth, or merely 'différentiellement lisse' (diagonal a regular immersion), a stratification of an O_S-module M is determined by its 1-connection. Any connection with zero curvature (a section of Ω²_{S/R}⊗End(M)) extends uniquely. Equivalently, Dér_{S/R} acts on M as a Lie-algebra action satisfying Leibniz. So stratified modules = integrable connections = modules over the Lie algebroid of derivations.

Two open questions are posed:
- how far smoothness is needed;
- whether an analogue holds for an arbitrary fibred category F (connections and curvature for general stacks).

Characteristic p: Cartier's theorem says a connection with zero p-curvature ('sans torsion, compatible avec puissances p-ièmes', added by hand) is equivalent to descent data along the relative Frobenius S → S^(p/R). Grothendieck stresses this is far from a stratification. This is implicitly the fact, later made precise by Katz and Gieseker, that stratifications in characteristic p are descent data along all Frobenius iterates.

1.10 begins: S of characteristic p, leading next page to absolute crystals, p-crystals F: M^(p)→M, and Dieudonné theory.
errors: The conjectured equivalence for flat, locally finitely presented S→R is doubtful as stated. Over a field every S of finite type is flat and finitely presented, so the claim would identify infinitesimal crystals with stratified coherent modules for every singular variety.

A plausible counterexample to that claim is a nodal curve or the cubic cone in characteristic 0. There, Kashiwara-type D-modules supported on S (= crystals) differ from modules over Grothendieck's ring of differential operators D_S, which is what stratifications see (Smith–Stafford; Ben-Zvi–Nevins; Bernstein–Gelfand–Gelfand on the cubic cone). I have not checked this in full.

The underlying reason the claim should fail: if S→R is not formally smooth, S need not cover the final object of the infinitesimal topos. A thickening of an open of S need not map to S, so values of a crystal are not reached by stratification data on S. Note that the finite flat case does work, e.g. k[x]/x² over k, where it reduces to fpqc descent.

This failure is consistent with Grothendieck's own caution ('Sauf erreur', proof not written). No error was found in the formally smooth / formally étale statements, nor in the characteristic-0 and Cartier statements.

ideas.what: Crystals in the infinitesimal site are equivalent to stratified modules when S→R is formally smooth
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.modern_name: Topological invariance / étale case of the infinitesimal site

ideas.what: Conjectured equivalence for flat, locally finitely presented S→R (R locally noetherian, coherent modules)
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of infinitesimal crystals with D_S-modules (Grothendieck differential operators) on singular schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later studied by Smith–Stafford and Ben-Zvi–Nevins in the D-module setting

ideas.what: In characteristic 0, smooth (or differentially smooth) case: stratification = integrable connection
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology; EGA IV 16 (différentiellement lisse)

ideas.what: Question whether connections and curvature make sense for an arbitrary fibred category F
ideas.modern_name: Connections on stacks / de Rham stack S_dR

ideas.what: Cartier: p-curvature-zero connections are equivalent to descent along relative Frobenius
Characteristic-p stratifications are much stronger than connections (implicit: descent along all Frobenius iterates)

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures without proof that crystals equal stratified objects for flat, locally finitely presented S→R. This is the question of comparing infinitesimal crystals with D_S-modules for singular schemes. Later D-module literature settled it largely negatively (non-unibranch singularities), but apparently without reference to this formulation.
missed.quote: Sauf erreur, on a encore une équivalence de catégories si S→R est plat et localement de présentation finie ... mais je n'ai pas écrit la démonstration.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor of the Smith–Stafford / Ben-Zvi–Nevins comparison of crystals with Grothendieck differential-operator modules on singular varieties. The likely failure is instructive. This is mainly of historical interest.

missed.claim: He asks whether the curvature criterion holds without smoothness, and for arbitrary fibred categories F. This anticipates connections on stacks and categories, i.e. the de Rham stack viewpoint.
missed.quote: J'ignore dans quelle mesure l'hypothèse de lissité est nécessaire ... ou si ... on peut formuler un énoncé analogue pour toute catégorie fibrée F sur (Sch)/R.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically it shows that the question of flat connections on general fibred categories / stacks was posed in 1966. It is now subsumed by derived and de Rham-stack formalisms.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. Its content was published in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' and cited by Berthelot. The only non-standard item is the unproved, probably false claim for flat finitely presented morphisms, plus a couple of open questions now absorbed into D-module and de Rham-stack theory.
transcription_corrections: 'ou k est de car. nulle' should read 'où k est de car. nulle'.
The marginal handwritten note reads approximately '"compatible avec puissances p-ièmes"' and attaches to 'connexion sans torsion sur M'.
'Module' has a handwritten mark over the 'o' (Grothendieck's capitalised 'Module' convention).
The interlinear handwritten insertion reads '(du moins si R loc. noeth., et se bornant aux Modules cohérents)'.
The final line ends with a struck-out word (probably 'le cas où' or similar); this is uncertain.
